title: Use a real preanchor to change the required number of grafting events
statement: For a Poisson(N) candidate population conditional on shared T~Exp(d), useful one-hit probability b*(1-exp(-k*T)), b=a*eta*theta*S in(0,1], and justified independent candidate thinning, let X=N*b. At k=d and X>0, no-link failure F1=(1-exp(-X))/X. For fixed integer m>=1 required surviving molecular links, Fm=(1/X)*sum_{j=0}^{m-1}P(j+1,X), with P the regularized lower incomplete gamma; Fm~m/X as X->infinity. At X=0 failure is1.

requires: A physically useful preanchor already associated with the new network, actual old/new contact and one additional old-side graft; no merely decorative association.
Conditional Poisson(N) candidates, fixed k,d>0 and independent candidate association/retention/targeting/individual service survival with justified joint probability b=a*eta*theta*S>0.
For the exact fixed-m gamma law k=d and m is a fixed positive integer; shared regional loss is a different failure model.

assumptions: The prior two-hit theorem stays valid; preanchoring is a new acquired prerequisite, not a free substitution.
Chemical count, structural load paths, shared delamination and equal resource costs are distinct. Rates and retention/targeting are unmeasured.
costs: Pay all preassociation, macromer/end supply, catalytic exposure, correct-side access and service retention. Smaller candidate count does not establish equal mass, energy, time or manufacturing cost.
contract.units: k,d are inverse time; X,N are dimensionless means; a,eta,theta,S are probabilities; P uses the regularized lower incomplete-gamma convention.
contract.obstruction: Acquire a useful persistent preanchor, old-side graft and actual joint lifetime law before importing the one-hit reliability gain.

body: At k=d, q=1-exp(-d*T) is uniform on[0,1]. Conditional useful count is Poisson(X*q); integrate its CDF below m and substitute z=X*q to obtain the gamma expression. This explains the changed N^-1 law versus the earlier two-hit N^-1/2 process: a real mechanically useful preanchor removes one required chemical event. At fixed arbitrary k/d=r>0, the one-link small-time linear law similarly gives F1~1/(r*X). These are not equal-mass/energy comparisons. Old-side targeting theta and individual later survival S multiply supply only under the declared candidate-thinning model. A guaranteed active T0>0 gives the m=1 bound F1<=exp(-X*(1-exp(-k*T0))) if enzyme, acceptor, water and contact genuinely persist. The original contact-first gate remains, and m molecular links need not be m independent load paths.
